title: The AI Trade Is Splitting Into Two Worlds, Goldman Sachs Says
key_facts: A Goldman Sachs note by strategists led by Kinger Lau, published Sunday 11 Oct 2026, says the narrative of a global AI duopoly is gaining traction among investors.
One ecosystem is centred on the US and its key trading partners; the other is forming in China, for geopolitical, national security and growth reasons.
Goldman cites breakthroughs by DeepSeek and Kimi in large language models and advances in semiconductor packaging, computing, biological engineering and aerospace.
China remains several generations behind at the leading edge of semiconductors but is 'probably on par with, or even leading' in parts of AI power, infrastructure, models and physical AI.
Goldman splits Chinese AI stocks into exporters tied to Western AI spending and domestic companies tied to China's own AI investment and policy support.
Chinese AI exporters gained 126% from early 2025 to June 2026, then fell 23% from their peak in the global AI selloff; domestic firms have held up better.

Since the 'DeepSeek moment' of early 2025, nearly $5 trillion of market value has been created in Chinese AI-related equities; AI-related stocks are 42% of the combined value of mainland and Hong Kong-listed Chinese stocks, up from 24% in 2024.
quote_evidence: One ecosystem is centered on the US and its key trading partners, while the other is taking shape in China, reflecting geopolitical, national security, and growth considerations, they wrote.
Chinese AI exporters gained 126% from early 2025 through June 2026 before falling 23% from their peak during the global AI selloff.
AI-related stocks now account for 42% of the combined stock market value of Chinese stocks listed in mainland China and Hong Kong, up from 24% in 2024, according to Goldman Sachs.
why_it_matters_hint: Goldman says investors should stop treating AI as one global trade.
event_date: Goldman note of 11 Oct 2026; Business Insider story of 13 Oct 2026
notes: Goldman's note itself was not found; the facts are Business Insider's account. The note was published Sunday 11 Oct 2026, so the story is older than the 13 Oct window start although Business Insider published on 13 Oct.
